22:["$","h2",null,{"children":"What the SAA is"}]
23:["$","p",null,{"children":["The SAA was instituted in 1975, at the time of local government reorganisation, as a voluntary body that brings together all of Scotland's Assessors and Electoral Registration Officers. Each Assessor is responsible, in their own area, for council tax banding, non-domestic (business) rating and the electoral register. The Association exists to share knowledge and keep practice consistent across those areas; it is the Assessors, not the Association, who make the individual banding decisions.",["$","a",null,{"className":"source-tick","href":"https://www.saa.gov.uk/","title":"SAA  –  Scottish Assessors Association (retrieved 2026-06-22)","target":"_blank","rel":"noopener nofollow","children":27}]]}]

25:["$","p",null,{"children":["The Scottish Assessors' Portal gives free public access to the Valuation Lists (council tax bands) and Valuation Rolls (rateable values) for eligible properties across Scotland. Enter a postcode or address and the portal returns the band the Assessor has assigned. If you disagree with a band you can make a proposal through the same site; strict time limits apply, so check the grounds and deadline before you start.",["$","a",null,{"className":"source-tick","href":"https://www.saa.gov.uk/council-tax/","title":"SAA  –  SAA Council Tax pages (retrieved 2026-06-22)","target":"_blank","rel":"noopener nofollow","children":28}]]}]
